$comment: Glowfin tuning data. Edited by designers, not programmers. Every value here is range-validated at load (src/core/config.ts) — a bad edit fails loudly at startup rather than producing subtly unfair gameplay. See docs/tuning-guide.md for what each value does.

audio.$comment: Part 3.5. One persistent allocation-bounded Web Audio graph: a calm bed is always present, moving-current and harmonic-shimmer layers enter from the same normalized momentum that drives speed/glow/trail, and transient sources are hard-capped. The AudioContext is created only by a real user gesture for iOS Safari.

visual.$comment: Caustic look. Exposed as tuning data so it can be iterated on-device with hot reload rather than guessed at. scale is cycles per world unit — too low and the pattern becomes one slow blob across the whole lane, which is exactly what the first version shipped with.

environment.$comment: Drowned city, god-rays and responsive coral. All three are instanced (one draw call each) because the draw budget is 90 and the scene already sits at 62. Everything here is BACKGROUND: it must never compete with obstacle silhouettes (Part 3.4), which is why buildings sit well outside the lane and coral is dim until it reacts.

creature.$comment: Part 3.1. Glowfin faces toward decreasing world Z into the obstacle corridor. The portrait chase camera sees its round back, manta fins, centered tail and three gill leaves per side. Both eyes sit high on the negative-Z front crown, ahead of the gills, and face the obstacle corridor rather than the chase camera. Their enlarged lenses remain readable at gameplay distance; a smoothed blend of momentum and actual forward speed drives their blue-to-rose colour response.

trail.$comment: Mesh ribbon, explicitly not particles (Part 3.3). segmentCount must stay at or under budgets.pools.maxTrailSegments.
